theme: God Is Near to Every Nation
summary: After Babel, Noah's descendants spread out into many nations. Among them was a family from Ur: Terah, his son Abram, and Abram's wife Sarai.

story_reel.narration: After Babel, people spread out across the whole earth. Families became tribes, and tribes became nations, each with its own language and land. Some went to the mountains, some to the deserts, some to the coasts. Genesis lists their names, like a giant family tree, because every family matters to God. One branch of Noah's family came through his son Shem. Many generations later, in a city called Ur, lived a man named Terah. Terah had a son named Abram. Abram married a woman named Sarai. But Sarai had no children, and that made her very sad. Terah took his family and set out toward a land called Canaan, but they stopped and settled in a place called Haran. God was watching this family closely. He had big plans for Abram. And the Bible tells us that God is not far from any of us, no matter what nation we come from.

memory_verse.text: he is not far from each one of us.

identity_focus.core_truth: Yahweh is near to me and to people from every nation.
identity_focus.reflection_prompt: God loves people from every nation, every language, and every family. Who is someone different from you that God loves too?

micro_prayer.text: Yahweh, thank You that You are near to everyone in every nation. Thank You for being near to me. Help me love people who are different from me. Amen.

companion.message: All these families came from my family long ago! Yahweh watched over every one. And now He's about to do something amazing through Abram.
